definition: A royal designation used for Ivan in tale no. 159.
cultural_caution: Do not flatten a Russian courtly title into ‘fighter,’ ‘prince class,’ or a universal fantasy rank.

definition: Royal female designations used respectively for Ivan’s sisters and for Marya Morevna in this tale.
cultural_caution: These labels are context-dependent social titles, not universal princess roles or game classes.

supports: The sisters are called царевна; Marya is called прекрасная королевна.

definition: The named opponent’s designation in tale no. 159; he is initially chained, regains strength through water, and is ultimately killed in this text.
cultural_caution: Do not translate the epithet into a stable lich, vampire, demon, or generic undead category. Koshchei figures vary across tale witnesses, and this text itself ends with his death.

supports: Koshchei’s designation, escape, and death appear in the tale.

literal_gloss: baba + Yaga; the phrase is not safely reducible to one English gloss
definition: The designated figure beyond the fire river who keeps horses and challenges Ivan in tale no. 159.
cultural_caution: Baba Yaga is not a stable pan-Slavic ‘witch race’ or automatic villain archetype. This record covers only the individual tale role in one Russian witness.

supports: Baba Yaga’s location, horse herd, test, iron mortar, and death are narrated.

definition: In this tale, dead water reunites Ivan’s body and living water revives him.
cultural_caution: The pair is an event-specific tale device here, not a standardized healing or resurrection spell system.

supports: The Raven uses dead water to reunite the body; the Falcon uses living water and Ivan rises.

definition: A tale-specific threshold crossed by a bridge created through Koshchei’s handkerchief and the site of Baba Yaga’s fall.
cultural_caution: This passage does not identify the fire river as a universal Slavic underworld, moral realm, or cosmological map.

supports: Koshchei describes the fire river; Ivan crosses it using the handkerchief bridge and Baba Yaga falls into it.

definition: Three uniquely designated avian suitors take human form in tale no. 159 and later perform distinct rescue actions.
cultural_caution: These specific form changes should not be extrapolated into a shared Slavic animal-person race or a general shapeshifter class.

supports: Each bird changes into a young man and the three later rescue Ivan.
